hints: The ball spends 3 s above the boy, half going up and half coming down. How fast must it be moving as it passes him?
worded:
1. The ball passes the top of the tower going up and again coming down, 3 s apart. By symmetry it takes 1.5 s from the boy up to its highest point.

2. To stop in 1.5 s under g, it must pass the boy at 15 m/s.

3. So between the ground and the top of the tower the speed falls from 25 to 15 m/s. That takes 1 s, at an average speed of 20 m/s: 20 m. (B)

4. Check: the top of the flight is 25²/20 = 31.25 m, and 15²/20 = 11.25 m above the tower top. 20 + 11.25 = 31.25. It fits.

**Another way: product of the two times.** The ball is at height h at two instants whose difference is 3 s and whose sum is the whole flight time 2 × 25/10 = 5 s. So the instants are 1 s and 4 s, and h = ½g × (1 × 4) = 20 m.
conventional:
![](asset:P000107-sol-1)

Take up as positive. The ball spends 3 s above the top of the tower, so by symmetry the speed there is

$$v = g\left( \frac{3}{2} \right) = 15\unit{m/s}.$$

From the ground to the top of the tower, using $v^{2} = u^{2} - 2gh$:

$$15^{2} = 25^{2} - 2(10)h\  \Rightarrow \ h = \frac{625 - 225}{20} = 20\unit{m}.$$
mistakes: The 3 s is spent above the boy (up and back down), so use 1.5 s, not 3 s, for the time to the top.
The tower height is not the maximum height (31.25 m); the ball goes 11.25 m above the boy.
